findings.title: SQL injection in migration via interpolated host value
findings.body: The migration builds an INSERT statement by string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value `h` comes directly from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting (line 22, `val.split("\n")`), which is admin-controlled free text. A host value containing a single quote (e.g. `x'); DROP TABLE users;--`) breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary SQL during `rake db:migrate`. This must use parameterized queries, e.g. `execute("INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)", h, category_id)` (or `exec_query` with binds). Note the same file's other `execute` calls interpolate only values read from the database itself (category id / setting value), which is lower risk, but the host loop is a direct injection path.

findings.title: update/destroy actions crash with NoMethodError when the host does not exist
findings.body: `update` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`, which dereferences `host.host = ...`. If no EmbeddableHost matches the id, `host` is nil and the request raises NoMethodError (500) instead of returning a 404. Same problem in `destroy` (line 15-16): `host.destroy` on nil raises. The controller should return `render_json_error`/404 (e.g. `raise Discourse::NotFound` or check `host.nil?`) when the record is missing. This is reachable by any admin via PUT/DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or bogus id, and the Ember client's `destroyRecord().then(...)` would surface an unhandled 500.

findings.title: Mass-assignment of arbitrary params into EmbeddableHost attributes
findings.body: `save_host` assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` directly from params without strong-parameter filtering or an allowlist. Any additional keys an admin POSTs under `embeddable_host[...]` are ignored only by luck of this explicit assignment, but more importantly there is no validation that `category_id` refers to an existing category before save; combined with `belongs_to :category` (no `validates :category, presence: true` on the model), an admin can set a dangling `category_id`. The model only validates the `host` format. Consider validating the category's existence (or at least that it is present) and using explicit permitted params.

findings.title: before_validation mutates nil host, crashing validation for blank hosts
findings.body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If `host` is nil (e.g. an admin submits an empty host field, or `EmbeddableHost.new` without a host), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, turning what should be a normal validation failure ("host is invalid") into a 500 error. The controller's `save_host` path (`EmbeddableHost.new` then assign from params) hits this whenever `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is blank/nil. Guard with `self.host = host.to_s` or `if host.present?` before the substitutions, and add `validates :host, presence: true` so blank input is rejected cleanly.

findings.title: record_for_host does case-insensitive lookup but stores mixed-case hosts, allowing duplicate/conflicting entries
findings.body: `record_for_host` matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but the column has no uniqueness constraint and the model has no uniqueness validation, so two rows `Example.com` and `example.com` can both exist (the migration even inserts raw setting values without normalization). `host_allowed?` then returns the first match, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` from an arbitrary one of them, so the category chosen for imported topics is nondeterministic. Add `validates :host, uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false }` and a unique index on `lower(host)` (or downcase in before_validation) so lookups are deterministic.

findings.title: Host validation regex is too permissive (allows paths, ports, and long TLDs), enabling referer-spoofing edge cases
findings.body: The format regex `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` permits an optional port and an arbitrary trailing path (`(\/.*)?`). However `record_for_host` compares only `uri.host`, ignoring port and path, so a stored host of `example.com:8080` or `example.com/evil` will authorize ANY referer whose host is `example.com` regardless of port/path. That silently widens the embed allowlist beyond what the admin configured (e.g. allowing `http://example.com:8080` or any path on that host). Either strip/normalize to host-only on save (the before_validation already strips scheme and path but not port) and reject ports, or make `record_for_host` compare scheme+host+port consistently. At minimum, the stored value should be normalized to a bare hostname and the regex should not accept `:` or `/`.

findings.title: Removing the 'embeddable hosts not set' guard lets embed/comments leak when no hosts are configured
findings.body: The old code raised `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set') if SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` before checking the referer. The new code only checks `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. `host_allowed?` returns `record_for_host(host).present?`, and `record_for_host` returns `false` when the referer is nil/unparseable — so with zero configured hosts every request is still denied. However, the behavior change is subtle and untested: previously a blank setting was an explicit early failure; now the security of the endpoint depends entirely on `record_for_host` correctly returning false for nil/blank referers (it does via `uri.present?` / `host.present?` checks, and `URI(nil)` raises and is rescued to nil). The spec at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb line 13-16 ('raises an error with a missing host') covers the no-host case, but there is no test for a nil referer with hosts configured in the 'by topic id' context — actually there is (line 35-38). The real gap: `ensure_embeddable` rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` already rescues internally and returns false, so the rescue is dead code; more importantly, if `request.referer` is nil, `URI(nil)` raises `TypeError` (not `InvalidURIError`) inside `record_for_host`... actually `URI(nil)` raises `ArgumentError`/`TypeError` depending on Ruby version — `URI(nil)` raises `TypeError: no implicit conversion of nil into String` in modern Ruby, which is NOT rescued by `rescue nil` modifier? The modifier `rescue nil` catches StandardError; TypeError is a StandardError, so it is caught. OK — but this fragility (relying on exception class coverage) should be replaced with an explicit `return false if host.blank?` guard in `record_for_host`/`host_allowed?`.

findings.title: EmbeddingSerializer serializes an OpenStruct, but has_many :embeddable_hosts with embed: :ids expects an association that OpenStruct does not provide
findings.body: `fetch_embedding` builds `@embedding = OpenStruct.new(id: 'default', embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host))`. `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`. ActiveModel::Serializers' `has_many` with `embed: :ids` calls `object.embeddable_hosts` (works on OpenStruct via method_missing) and then maps to ids — this likely works, but `embed: :ids` means the response only contains `embeddable_host_ids: [...]` and NOT the embedded host objects. The Ember route does `this.store.find('embedding')` and the template iterates `embedding.embeddable_hosts` expecting full host objects with `host.host` and `host.category`. With `embed: :ids`, the store's `_hydrateEmbedded` (store.js.es6) looks up `root['embeddable_hosts']` (plural collection) in the payload — which is absent because ids-only embedding produces `embeddable_host_ids`. The `_lookupSubType` for the `embeddable_host_ids` key (matching `/(.+)_id(s?)$/`) will try to find each id in `root['embeddable_hosts']`, which is undefined, so `hydrated` will be `[undefined, ...]` and `obj['embeddable_hosts'] = [undefined...]`. The admin UI will render broken/empty rows. The serializer should use `embed: :objects` (or embed the objects with their serializer) so the payload contains an `embeddable_hosts` array, matching what the Ember store and template expect.

findings.title: save() sends only the 'host' property, dropping category_id from the buffered changes and never persisting category edits
findings.body: `const props = this.get('buffered').getProperties('host');` fetches only the `host` key from the buffer, then `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` is set on the props object. But `categoryId` is a separate component property bound to the `category-chooser`, and it is only initialized in the `edit()` action (`this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))`). For a NEW host (created via `addHost`), `edit()` is never called, so `categoryId` stays `null`; when saving, `props.category_id = null` is sent, and the server-side `save_host` then defaults it to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` (controller line 25). So a newly added host can never be assigned a non-default category through the UI — the category chooser selection is silently discarded on create. Additionally, `getProperties('host')` returns the buffered host string, and assigning `props.category_id` mutates that plain object correctly, but if the buffer contained more keys they'd be dropped. The fix: build props explicitly, e.g. `const props = { host: this.get('buffered.host'), category_id: this.get('categoryId') }`, and initialize `categoryId` for new records (or bind the chooser directly to `buffered.category_id`).

findings.title: After save, category is set from a possibly-null categoryId, desyncing the model from the server response
findings.body: After a successful save, the code does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`. If `categoryId` is null (new host saved without choosing a category — see related finding), `findById(null)` returns undefined and the host's `category` is set to undefined even though the server defaulted `category_id` to the uncategorized category. The server response (serialized with `rest_serializer: true`) contains the authoritative `category_id`, but it is ignored. The component should rely on the save response / `host.reload()` or at least fall back to the server-provided `category_id` rather than the possibly-stale local `categoryId`.

findings.title: saveChanges action calls update({}) with no attributes and has no UI trigger
findings.body: `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` — an empty attribute hash. The `embedding` model is an OpenStruct-backed singleton with only `id` and `embeddable_hosts`; there are no editable scalar attributes on the embedding itself (all settings like embed_truncate remain site settings). The template (embedding.hbs) has no button wired to `saveChanges`, so this action is dead code that would issue a pointless PUT /admin/customize/embedding with an empty payload if ever invoked. Either remove the action or wire it to actual embedding-level settings; as written it is misleading dead code.

findings.title: basePath type normalization breaks existing admin models whose type key uses underscores
findings.body: `basePath` now does `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))`. `String.replace` with a string pattern replaces only the FIRST occurrence, and more importantly the check is applied to the raw `type` passed from the store. For the existing admin model `site-customization`, the store type key is `site-customization` (already dashed) so it still matches. But for `plugin` it matches. The new `embeddable-host` type is dashed, so it matches. However, if any caller uses the underscored form `embeddable_host` (e.g. `store.createRecord('embeddable_host')` as done in admin-embedding.js.es6 line 10!), `type.replace('_', '-')` converts it to `embeddable-host` and it matches — OK. But `Ember.String.underscore(store.pluralize(type))` in `pathFor` will pluralize `embeddable_host` to `embeddable_hosts` and underscore to `embeddable_hosts`, producing `/admin/embeddable_hosts` — while the Rails route is `resources :embeddable_hosts` under the admin namespace, which by default maps to `/admin/embeddable_hosts` — that matches. The subtle break: `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore; a type like `foo_bar_baz` becomes `foo-bar_baz` and won't match a dashed ADMIN_MODELS entry. This is fragile; use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')` or `Ember.String.dasherize(type)` for correctness.

findings.title: _hydrateEmbedded maps plural _ids keys without guarding against non-array values, producing [undefined] entries
findings.body: The new plural branch does `obj[k].map(...)` whenever the key matches `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with the `s` group. If a serializer sends `category_ids: null` or a non-array (e.g. a single id, or an empty string), `.map` either throws (null) or iterates characters (string), corrupting the hydrated object. There is no `Ember.isArray(obj[k])` guard. The single-id branch guards with `if (hydrated)`, but the plural branch assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` where `hydrated` is the result of `.map` — if `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for a missing id, the array contains `undefined` entries rather than being filtered. This affects the new `embeddable_host_ids` embedding path (see EmbeddingSerializer finding): when the payload contains `embeddable_host_ids` but no `embeddable_hosts` collection, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for each id and the model ends up with `embeddable_hosts = [undefined, undefined, ...]`. Add an `Ember.isArray` check and filter out undefined lookups.

findings.title: Serializer exposes only category_id, but the Ember component reads host.category (object) for display and editing
findings.body: `EmbeddableHostSerializer` emits `id, host, category_id`. The Ember component `embeddable-host.js.es6` reads `this.get('host.category.id')` in `edit()` and the template renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`. With only `category_id` serialized (and the embedding payload using `embed: :ids` per the EmbeddingSerializer), the store's `_hydrateEmbedded` will attempt to resolve `category_id` via `_lookupSubType('category', ...)`, which special-cases categories via `Discourse.Category.findById(id)` — this works only if the category is already loaded client-side. For an admin page where categories may not be preloaded, `host.category` will be undefined and the badge renders blank, and `edit()` sets `categoryId` to undefined. The serializer should include the category object (e.g. `has_one :category` or a `category` attribute with BasicCategorySerializer) when `rest_serializer` is used for the embedding payload, or the component should use `host.category_id` directly with the category-chooser.

findings.title: Category fabricators were moved into the wrong file, leaving category_fabricator.rb containing only the embeddable_host fabricator
findings.body: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was gutted: all category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were deleted from it and now that file contains ONLY `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. Meanwhile `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` was created containing the category fabricators (and NOT the embeddable_host fabricator). The two files' contents are swapped. This means: (1) `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` is defined in `category_fabricator.rb` — it will load, but the file name is wrong and confusing; (2) more critically, the `:embeddable_host` fabricator references `category` (line 3: `category`), which requires the `:category` fabricator — that now lives in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Fabrication loads all files in spec/fabricators, so both will be loaded and it may work by accident, but the file naming is inverted: `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` should contain the embeddable_host fabricator and `category_fabricator.rb` should contain the category fabricators. This is clearly a copy-paste/file-swap mistake that will confuse maintainers and risks load-order issues.

findings.title: embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains category fabricators instead of the embeddable_host fabricator
findings.body: This file is named `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` but its entire content is the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) — the exact content that was removed from `category_fabricator.rb`. The actual `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` block (host "eviltrout.com", category) was placed in `category_fabricator.rb` instead. The two files have been swapped. Every spec that does `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` (embed_controller_spec, topic_embed_spec, topic_spec, embeddable_host_spec) depends on this fabricator being correctly defined and associated with a category; while Fabrication loads all fabricator files so it may resolve, the misplacement is a clear defect: the embeddable_host fabricator belongs in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, and the category fabricators belong in category_fabricator.rb. Fix by swapping the file contents back.

findings.title: Authorization relies on redundant before_filter in addition to Admin::AdminController and route constraint
findings.body: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` inherits from `Admin::AdminController` (which already enforces staff access) and the route is declared with `constraints: AdminConstraint.new` (admin-only, routes.rb line 153). The explicit `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` on line 3 is redundant — it downgrades the effective protection from admin-only (route constraint) to staff-only (moderators) at the controller layer. A moderator hitting the controller directly (if the route constraint were ever relaxed or bypassed) would pass `ensure_staff` but should not manage embeddable hosts. Other admin controllers in this codebase (e.g. permalinks, emojis) rely on the AdminConstraint route constraint and Admin::AdminController without re-declaring ensure_staff. Remove the redundant filter or change it to `ensure_admin` for defense in depth consistent with the AdminConstraint.

findings.title: TopicEmbed.import silently creates topics in the uncategorized category when no EmbeddableHost matches the URL
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` now does `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` to PostCreator. `record_for_host` returns `false` (not nil) when the URL is unparseable or has no host, and returns `nil` when no DB row matches. `eh.try(:category_id)` on `false` returns nil (false doesn't respond to category_id, try returns nil), and on nil returns nil. So for any embed URL whose host is not in the allowlist, `category` is nil and PostCreator falls back to the default/uncategorized category. Previously the category came from the `embed_category` site setting, which was a single global default. Now, if an admin has not configured an EmbeddableHost for a feed URL, imported topics silently land in uncategorized instead of the configured embed category — a behavior regression for existing sites upgrading (the migration only creates EmbeddableHost rows from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting, and deletes `embed_category`; sites that relied on `embed_category` without listing every feed host in `embeddable_hosts` lose their category assignment). The import path should either reject URLs without a matching EmbeddableHost (since TopicRetriever already gates on `host_allowed?`) or fall back to a sensible default explicitly.

findings.title: expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable host exists, changing behavior for sites with no hosts configured
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. The `embeddable_hosts.present?` guard was removed because the setting no longer exists. But the semantic of that guard was: only offer the 'expand embed' UI when embedding is actually enabled on the site (at least one allowed host). Now, on a site with zero EmbeddableHost rows, any topic that has a TopicEmbed (e.g. created via feed polling before hosts were removed, or imported by other means) will show the expandable first-post UI even though no external site is allowed to embed it. The correct replacement guard is `EmbeddableHost.exists?` (or checking that the topic's embed_url host is allowed). The spec was updated to fabricate an embeddable_host in the 'with an embeddable host' context, confirming the intent, but the production code lost the check entirely.

findings.title: Controller spec only checks inheritance; no tests for create/update/destroy behavior or authorization
findings.body: The entire spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController is a single assertion that the class is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. There are no tests for: creating a host (happy path + validation failure), updating a host, destroying a host, the nil-record 500 bug (see controller finding), authorization (non-staff/non-admin rejected), or the category_id defaulting to uncategorized when blank. Given this controller performs writes against a security-sensitive allowlist (embeddable hosts control which external sites can iframe the forum), the absence of any behavioral or authorization test is a significant gap. At minimum, add tests mirroring other admin controller specs: admin can create/update/destroy, moderator is denied (route constraint is AdminConstraint), invalid host returns 422, missing id returns 404 (once fixed).

findings.title: Embedding controller spec only checks inheritance; show/update serialization untested
findings.body: Like the embeddable_hosts spec, this spec contains only `expect(Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`. The `show` action's serialization (EmbeddingSerializer with the OpenStruct, embed: :ids behavior) and the `update` action are completely untested. Given the serializer/store contract concerns around `embed: :ids` vs the Ember client expecting embedded objects (see EmbeddingSerializer finding), a serialization spec asserting the JSON shape of GET /admin/customize/embedding is essential. Add a test that GETs the show action as admin and asserts the response contains the expected structure (embeddable_hosts with id/host/category_id), and that non-admins are rejected.

findings.title: update action is a no-op that re-renders show; PUT /admin/customize/embedding accepts and ignores any payload
findings.body: `update` simply re-renders the embedding serializer without reading or applying any params. The route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` (routes.rb line 139) accepts a PUT with an arbitrary body and returns 200 with the current embedding state, silently discarding whatever the client sent. The Ember adapter's `update` (rest.js.es6 line 56) sends `data[typeField] = attrs` and expects `json[typeField]` back. This is a misleading API: clients may believe settings were saved. Either implement actual update semantics (e.g. accept embed_truncate and other embedding settings) or remove the PUT route and the `saveChanges` controller action to avoid a dead, misleading endpoint.

findings.title: resources :embeddable_hosts generates an index/show route that has no controller action
findings.body: `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` generates all RESTful routes including GET /admin/embeddable_hosts (index) and GET /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id (show). `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` only defines `create`, `update`, and `destroy` — there are no `index` or `show` actions. A request to those routes will raise AbstractController::ActionNotFound (or UnknownFormat) → 500/404. Since the Ember client fetches hosts via the embedding endpoint (GET /admin/customize/embedding), the index/show routes are unnecessary. Restrict the resource: `resources :embeddable_hosts, only: [:create, :update, :destroy], constraints: AdminConstraint.new`.

findings.title: Template hides the entire hosts table (and shows nothing) when there are zero hosts, with no empty-state message
findings.body: `{{#if embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` wraps the whole table. When no hosts exist, the admin sees only the 'Add Host' button with no explanation, and — combined with the EmbeddingSerializer `embed: :ids` issue — `embedding.embeddable_hosts` may be undefined or an array of undefined entries even when hosts exist, causing the table to render with broken rows or not at all. Add an `{{else}}` branch with an empty-state message (e.g. i18n 'admin.embedding.no_hosts'), and ensure the serializer actually embeds host objects so the `if` evaluates correctly.

findings.title: @on('didInsertElement') combined with @observes('editing') refocuses the input on every edit toggle, fighting user interaction
findings.body: The `_focusOnInput` method is decorated with both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`. The observer fires whenever `editing` changes (i.e., when entering AND leaving edit mode). When leaving edit mode (editing becomes false), the observer still schedules `this.$('.host-name').focus()` in afterRender — but by then the input may no longer exist (the `{{#if editing}}` block has been torn down), so `this.$('.host-name')` is an empty jQuery set and `.focus()` is a no-op; harmless but sloppy. More importantly, the observer firing on `editing` becoming false is unintended. The intent is clearly to focus only when entering edit mode. Use `@observes('editing')` with a guard `if (this.get('editing'))`, or better, drop the observer and call the focus logic explicitly from the `edit()` action and `didInsertElement` when `host.isNew`.

findings.title: destroyRecord failure leaves the host in the list and gives no feedback beyond the generic ajax error popup
findings.body: In the `delete` action, `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); })` only removes the host from the controller's list on success. There is no `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (unlike `save`), so if the DELETE request fails (e.g. the nil-record 500 from the controller, or a network error), the promise rejection is unhandled — no error is shown to the admin and the row stays. The user gets no feedback that deletion failed. Add `.catch(popupAjaxError)` to match the `save` action's error handling.

findings.title: No test for blank/nil host (the before_validation nil crash) and no uniqueness validation test
findings.body: The spec tests trimming of http/https/paths and host_allowed? matching, but does not test: (1) `EmbeddableHost.new(host: nil).valid?` or `EmbeddableHost.new(host: '').valid?` — which currently crashes with NoMethodError in before_validation (see model finding); (2) duplicate host rejection (case-insensitive) — the model has no uniqueness validation; (3) that `record_for_host` returns false for nil/blank/unparseable input (the security-critical path used by EmbedController#ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever). Adding these tests would pin down the nil-crash bug and the case-insensitive duplicate issue.

findings.title: count action renders JSONP with unvalidated callback parameter (pre-existing, but now more exposed without host gate context)
findings.body: `render json: {counts: by_url}, callback: params[:callback]` reflects the `callback` query parameter directly into a JSONP response. While this is pre-existing code and not changed by this PR, the PR removes the `embeddable_hosts` blank-check from `ensure_embeddable` (which also gates `count`), meaning the JSONP reflection is now reachable in configurations where previously a blank setting would have blocked it. A malicious `callback` value could be used for reflected content injection in browsers that render the response as HTML (JSONP callback injection). This should be validated against a whitelist regex (e.g. `/\A[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*\z/`) or removed in favor of CORS. Flagging because the PR's change to `ensure_embeddable` alters the exposure of this endpoint.

findings.title: category-chooser bound to categoryId which is not initialized for new records, so new hosts cannot pick a category
findings.body: The `{{category-chooser value=categoryId}}` binds to the component's `categoryId` property, which is initialized to `null` (component line 9) and only set in the `edit()` action. For a new host row (created via `addHost` → `store.createRecord('embeddable-host')`), `edit()` is never invoked (the row starts in editing mode because `host.isNew` is true), so `categoryId` remains null. The chooser shows no selection, and on save `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` sends null, which the server replaces with the uncategorized category. The admin's category selection for a new host is therefore always ignored. Initialize `categoryId` when the host is new (e.g. in `didInsertElement` if `host.isNew`, set it to the default/uncategorized category id) or bind the chooser to `buffered.category_id` so it participates in the buffer lifecycle.

findings.title: Migration reads embed_category by joining site_settings.value to categories.name, which fails for renamed categories or non-default locales
findings.body: The migration resolves the target category with `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`. This joins the site setting's value (a category NAME) to `categories.name`. If the category was renamed after the setting was configured, or if the setting holds a slug rather than a name, or if multiple categories share a name (possible in different parents), the join returns zero or multiple rows. `[0]['id']` on an empty result raises NoMethodError (nil['id']), aborting the migration. The fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` only triggers when `category_id == 0`, not when the query crashes. More robust: look up by name with `Category.where(name: value).first` semantics, or rescue and default. Also, the migration deletes the `embed_category` and `embeddable_hosts` settings at the end (line 31) — if the INSERT loop fails midway (e.g. SQL injection crash or constraint violation), the settings are NOT deleted (good), but partial embeddable_hosts rows may already be inserted, and re-running the migration will duplicate them (no uniqueness constraint). Consider wrapping in a transaction (migrations are transactional by default in Rails, but `execute` DDL/DML is fine) and adding a uniqueness guard.

findings.title: Plural _ids hydration assigns undefined entries instead of filtering missing lookups
findings.body: In the new plural branch of `_hydrateEmbedded`, `obj[k].map(function(id) { return self._lookupSubType(subType, type, id, root); })` — when `_lookupSubType` returns undefined (id not found in the root collection), the resulting array contains `undefined` holes. The subsequent `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` keeps those holes. Downstream code iterating `embeddable_hosts` (e.g. the `{{#each}}` in embedding.hbs) will render rows for `undefined` entries, causing template errors (`Cannot read property 'host' of undefined`). The single-id branch guards with `if (hydrated)`, but the plural branch has no equivalent filter. Add `.filter(function(h) { return !!h; })` or use `Ember.A()` with compact semantics.

findings.title: Locale string 'Allowed Hosts' is used as a table column header for a single host value
findings.body: The locale key `admin.embedding.host: "Allowed Hosts"` (plural) is used in embedding.hbs line 4 as the column header for the host column (`{{i18n "admin.embedding.host"}}`). A column listing individual hostnames should be singular ("Host" or "Allowed Host"), not plural "Allowed Hosts". The plural reads incorrectly as a section title. Change to `host: "Host"` (or "Allowed Host") for the column header.

findings.title: Silent fallback to uncategorized_category_id when category_id is blank may hide admin configuration errors
findings.body: `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` silently substitutes the uncategorized category whenever the client sends a blank/nil category_id. Combined with the Ember component bug (categoryId not initialized for new hosts), this means a new host created without explicitly choosing a category is silently assigned to uncategorized — the admin may believe they set a category that was never sent. While the fallback prevents a NOT NULL violation (category_id is null: false in the migration), it masks client/server contract mismatches. Consider returning a validation error when category_id is blank on create (forcing the UI to send a valid category), or at minimum ensure the UI always sends a valid category_id (see component finding).
